previous_statement: The defining dagger condition for an extended d-inclusion makes v dagger-preserving, and w_doubleprime(X)=w_prime(X^dagger)^dagger makes w=(w_prime+w_doubleprime)/2 dagger-preserving, so v^+=v+w is dagger-preserving. Put mu=105(d^2+epsilon), x=v^+(I_B), and y=x-I_A. From ||v^+-v||<=2d and the d-unit bound for v, ||y||<=3d. Multiplicativity gives ||x^2-x||<=mu. Expanding x=I_A+y and using the approximate-unit and product inequalities gives ||y||<=mu+epsilon(1+epsilon)+2epsilon||y||+(1+epsilon)||y||^2. If d+epsilon<=1/16, then ||y||<=3/16 and the last two terms are absorbed, yielding ||y||<=4(mu+epsilon)<=424(d^2+epsilon). The unit of M_n tensor B maps to I_n tensor x, and the operator-space axioms give ||I_n tensor y||=||y||; hence every amplification has unit defect at most C_u(d^2+epsilon) with C_u=424.
new_statement: Let v^+=v+w, where v is dagger-preserving, w_doubleprime(X)=w_prime(X^dagger)^dagger, and w=(w_prime+w_doubleprime)/2. Assume the two estimates supplied separately by the correction branches: sup_n ||I_n tensor w|| <= 2d and, at every amplification, ||v_n^+(XY)-v_n^+(X)v_n^+(Y)|| <= 105(d^2+epsilon)||X||||Y||. Then v^+ is dagger-preserving. Put q=d^2+epsilon, mu=105q, x=v^+(I_B), and y=x-I_A. The level-one displacement estimate and the d-unit bound for v give ||y|| <= 3d, while the multiplicative estimate at X=Y=I_B gives ||x^2-x|| <= mu. Expanding x=I_A+y and isolating y gives ||y|| <= mu+epsilon(1+epsilon)+2epsilon||y||+(1+epsilon)||y||^2. If d+epsilon <= 1/16, then ||y|| <= 3/16 and 2epsilon+(1+epsilon)||y|| <= 83/256; hence ||y|| <= (272/173)(mu+epsilon) < 4(mu+epsilon) <= 424q. Finally I_n tensor y is the block diagonal direct sum of n copies of y, so the operator-space direct-sum axiom gives ||I_n tensor y||=||y||. Thus every amplification has unit defect at most 424(d^2+epsilon).
